newsitem.title: USA: LIFFE chairman sees volume doubling in five years.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE chairman sees volume doubling in five years.

text.p: Volume at the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange could double in the next five years, the chairman of the exchange said on Wednesday.

"I can easily see our volume doubling in a five-year period and I can see us possibly overtaking each of the big Chicago...(futures) exchanges," LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth told reporters at a press luncheon here.
He called the exchange "fairly neck-and-neck" with volume at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange already.
"We may be the biggest individual exchange in the world within five years," Wigglesworth said, adding that LIFFE volume probably would not exceed the combined volume of the Chicago exchanges.
Wigglesworth reiterated that a strategic link with the Chicago Board of Trade would commence on May 9, 1997.
Under the linkage, the CBOT and LIFFE will each trade the other's major fixed-income financial futures contract on their respective floors by open outcry.
As for talks between the CBOT and the CME to combine back office and trade processing operations, Wigglesworth said he saw no impact from those talks on LIFFE's linkage with the CBOT.
